claims.text: tron is the inference program this code belongs to; every type in this file lives in namespace tron.

fields.definition: The inference program under test (the project's CLAUDE.md term list). Every type of this header is declared inside namespace tron.

claims.text: TRON_K_VNNI is the CMake option that switches the K plane of every 128-dimension head to the VNNI layout; its compile-time gate is k_vnni::layout_on<head_size>.

fields.definition: A CMake option (default OFF, requires TRON_AMX_DISPATCH). When defined, layout_on<128> is true and the K plane of every 128-dimension head holds the VNNI layout; every other head size keeps the row-major plane.

claims.text: AMX is the CPU's tile instruction set; one panel of the plane is exactly one AMX B tile.

fields.definition: Advanced Matrix Extensions, the tile instruction set of the CPU. Its tile multiply TDPBF16PS consumes the VNNI layout as its B operand (the second matrix of the multiply); one 1 KiB panel is one B tile.

claims.text: bf16 is the 16-bit brain floating-point format; every K value is one bf16, so a 128-dimension row is 256 bytes.

fields.definition: The 16-bit brain floating-point format. A bf16 shifted up by 16 bits is the exact fp32 (32-bit float). One 128-dimension K row is 128 bf16 = 256 bytes.

claims.text: A page holds 64 tokens of K and V; it is a lightweight reference to a section of a book.

fields.definition: The unit of KV storage: 64 contiguous tokens. The attention computation proceeds page by page. A page struct is a lightweight reference to a section of a book; the client does not construct pages directly.

claims.text: A book is the unit of memory allocation that owns the KV memory of a requested number of pages and hands out page references.

fields.definition: The unit of memory allocation of the KV cache. It reserves space for a requested number of pages, owns that memory, creates all the pages it will need when constructed, and hands out references to them on demand.

claims.text: A KV head is one key/value head of the attention; a kv_block is the KV cache for one KV head in one KV slot, and kv_mul query heads share one KV head.

fields.definition: One key/value head of grouped-query attention. One kv_block is the KV cache for one KV head in one KV slot. kv_mul is the number of query heads that share one KV head; qk_group scores them in passes of up to 16 heads.

claims.text: A plane is K for one KV head of one page: 64 tokens x 128 dimensions of bf16 = 16 KiB.

fields.definition: K for one KV head of one page: 64 tokens x 128 dimensions of bf16 = 16 KiB, the same bytes as the row-major plane. kv_block::k is the plane's owner (k_vnni_tensor) for a VNNI slot.

claims.text: EAGLE is a separate KV storage with its own layout-state entry at index layout_t::n_slots; k_state_ix maps slot zero to it while the EAGLE view is active.

fields.definition: A KV storage that follows the active retained slots (used by the EAGLE speculative-decoding draft). It has one extra K layout state entry (index layout_t::n_slots, EAGLE_STORAGE_SLOTS_1). k_state_ix returns that entry for slot zero while the EAGLE view is active.

claims.text: A panel is one (dimension step, token block): 16 dimension-pair rows of 64 bytes = 1 KiB, exactly one AMX B tile; a plane has 16 panels.

fields.definition: One (s, c) pair of the plane: 16 dimension-pair rows of 64 bytes = 1 KiB (PANEL_BYTES_1024). A panel is exactly one AMX B tile. A plane has N_PANELS_16 = 4 steps x 4 blocks panels; the 4 panels of one token block occupy 4 KiB.

claims.text: A pair row is one 64-byte line holding one dimension pair for the 16 tokens of a block: 32 bf16 = 16 dwords.

fields.definition: One 64-byte line of a panel: one dimension pair for 16 consecutive tokens, 32 bf16 = 16 dwords (ROW_ELEMS_32, ROW_DWORDS_16). The 16 pair rows of a panel are 64 bytes apart (pair_row_offsets).

claims.text: A dimension pair (dp) is two consecutive dimensions of one token that share one 32-bit lane (dword).

fields.definition: Dimensions 2 dp and 2 dp + 1 of one token, stored together in one 32-bit lane (a dword, DWORD_BYTES_4). A 512-bit register has LANES_16 such lanes, one per token of a block.

claims.text: A dimension step (s) is 32 dimensions = 16 dimension pairs, the depth of one AMX tile multiply; a 128-dimension head has 4 steps.

fields.definition: 32 dimensions = 16 dimension pairs (STEP_DIMS_32, STEP_PAIRS_16): the depth of one AMX tile multiply. HEAD_SIZE_128 / STEP_DIMS_32 = DIM_STEPS_4 steps per head.

claims.text: A token block (c) is 16 consecutive tokens of a page (page offsets 16 c .. 16 c + 15); a page has 4 blocks and each block's 4 panels occupy 4 KiB.

fields.definition: 16 consecutive tokens of a page (BLOCK_TOKENS_16), page offsets 16 c .. 16 c + 15. A page has TOKEN_BLOCKS_4 blocks. The block's bytes are its 4 panels (one per dimension step), 4 KiB in all, whether the block is row-major or VNNI.

claims.text: Row-major (native) K stores one row of head_size bf16 per token; it is the layout of every non-128 head and of an incomplete block.

fields.definition: One row of head_size bf16 values per token, indexed [p * head_size + i]. Every head size other than 128 keeps this plane; inside a VNNI plane an incomplete 16-token block holds its rows this way (Note [Row-major tail block]).

claims.text: A row-major tail block is a 16-token block that holds its rows row-major until all 16 rows are saved and the block is converted in place.

fields.definition: A 16-token block of a VNNI plane whose rows are stored row-major (token t owns 256 contiguous bytes in panel (t / 4, c), row t % 4) until all 16 K rows are saved; block_to_vnni then transposes it in place. The page's converted-block bit says which form a block holds.

claims.text: A transfer row (const_k_row_view / k_row_view) is one token's head_size bf16 in dimension order with the caller's alignment and DMA flags; it is not packed storage.

fields.definition: A rank-1 typed view of one token's Cols bf16 values in dimension order, carrying the caller's Aligned and Dma flags (defaults VIEW_ALIGNED_TRUE, VIEW_DMA_FALSE). It is the argument type of page::set_k_row / get_k_row and of store_row / load_row.

claims.text: A page offset is a token's position inside its 64-token page (0..63); offset_bit(offset) is its bit in the saved-rows word.

fields.definition: A token's position inside its 64-token page, 0..63. Its block is offset / 16 and its lane is offset % 16. k_rows_saved_ keeps one bit per page offset; offset_bit(offset) is that bit.

claims.text: k_vnni_blocks_ (read through page::k_vnni_blocks) is the page's per-slot byte with one bit per 16-token block: the blocks that hold the VNNI layout.

fields.definition: Per storage slot, one bit per 16-token block (bit c = page offsets 16 c .. 16 c + 15): the converted blocks that hold the VNNI layout. Every reader and writer of a row takes the row's layout from this bit. A page is dense for the AMX kernel when the byte equals BLOCKS_PER_PAGE_MASK_0XF.

claims.text: A scatter writes the 16 dwords of one register to 16 addresses given by an offset vector; a gather reads them. store_row issues 4 scatters, load_row 4 gathers.

fields.definition: _mm512_i32scatter_epi32 writes the 16 dwords of one register to base + 16 offsets; _mm512_i32gather_epi32 reads 16 dwords from such addresses. store_row scatters one token's 16 dimension pairs per step into the 16 pair rows of a panel (4 scatters, 64 lines touched); load_row is the inverse.

claims.text: A block save (store_block, page::set_k_block) stores a run of 16 tokens that fills one block: the rows are transposed in registers and written as 64 whole 64-byte lines in the VNNI layout.

fields.definition: The store of a run of 16 consecutive tokens that fills one 16-token block (store_block, page::set_k_block): transposed in registers and written as whole lines, directly in the VNNI layout. The caller then publishes the 16 row bits and the block bit with note_k_block_saved. Prefill saves blocks this way.

claims.text: The forward end is the point after the plugin joined its workers and the cooperative GOF staging drained: the first point where no reader of this pass is left, where convert_pending_k_blocks converts the queued blocks.

fields.definition: The end of a forward pass, after the plugin's run() returned and wait_for_coop_gof drained the cooperative GOF staging. It is the first point where no reader of this pass is left, so the main thread converts the blocks that short runs completed (convert_pending_k_blocks -> k_block_to_vnni_at).

claims.text: In decode every step saves one token per user, a run shorter than a block stored row-major; prefill stores whole blocks.

fields.definition: Decode: the generation phase where every step saves one token per user, so the tail block of every user is stored row by row (set_k_row) and read again on every step. Prefill: the prompt phase whose runs of 16 tokens fill whole blocks (set_k_block).

claims.text: k_vnni::qk_group is the AVX-512 score reader of the VNNI layout: one token per vector lane, no gather and no horizontal reduction; it serves partial pages, hosts without AMX and the kill switch.

fields.definition: The AVX-512 QK reader of the VNNI plane (h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp). One 64-byte load supplies one dimension pair of 16 tokens; the query's pair is broadcast and VDPBF16PS accumulates 16 scores at once. It scores only tokens whose `live` bit is set and whose block is VNNI; it is one of the two readers allowed to take the plane address.

claims.text: qk_vnni_128x4 is the AMX dense QK kernel: the page's 16 K panels are the B operand and the padded 4 query rows the A operand, giving S = Q . K^T for one whole page without a transpose.

fields.definition: The AMX kernel that scores one dense page whose K is stored in the VNNI layout: S = Q . K^T with the padded query rows as the A operand and the 16 K panels as the B operand, writing s[4][64] fp32 unscaled. It takes page::k_packed and is the second reader allowed to take the plane address.

claims.text: The dense AMX path is taken per (query, page) only when the whole 64-token page is active, visible and inside the sliding window, and with VNNI K only when every block of the page is converted.

fields.definition: The AMX fast path of software attention for one (query, page) pair: the page must be a full 64-token page wholly visible to the query (is_dense_amx_page), a packed Q must exist, and with VNNI K page::k_vnni_blocks must equal BLOCKS_PER_PAGE_MASK_0XF. Every other pair runs the AVX-512 software loop.

claims.text: The kill switch TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1 makes AMX unavailable at run time; with TRON_K_VNNI the layout stays VNNI and qk_group scores it, so it is an AMX-off run of the same layout.

fields.definition: TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1 in the environment makes available() false, so no AMX kernel runs. It does not change the K layout: a TRON_K_VNNI binary then reads the VNNI blocks with the AVX-512 reader qk_group, not the row-major dotter, and both store paths are untouched.

claims.text: Hardware attention means the FPGA scores an operation's K; under it save_k records no row bits and the blocks decode completes stay row-major.

fields.definition: Attention scored on the FPGA for an operation (cached_operation_uses_hw, decided once per model). For such an operation save_k records no row bits for short runs and queues no block for conversion, so those blocks stay row-major; the CPU scores only the tail tokens above the FPGA's coverage.
fields.source: Note [Row-major blocks under hardware attention] (kv_cache.hpp:729-764); model.hpp:1530-1533

claims.text: A GOF is a group of four consecutive tokens whose K/V rows the staging copies into a buffer that DMA moves to the FPGA card.

fields.definition: A group of four consecutive tokens. The staging (gof::populate) copies their K/V rows into a buffer that DMA moves to the FPGA card. The cooperative GOF staging gather of an earlier minibatch can still read a block's rows row-major while a later minibatch saves the block's last rows.

claims.text: The FPGA staging path (gof::populate -> shuffle_k_entry) needs one row per token: for a row-major block it takes the row pointer from page::k_row_if_row_major with no copy; for a converted block it gathers the row with page::get_k_row.

fields.definition: The copy of K/V rows into the DMA buffer for the FPGA (gof::populate -> shuffle_k_entry), one row per token. page_info::k_head_fn returns the in-place row from page::k_row_if_row_major for a row-major block, and gathers the row into caller-owned scratch with page::get_k_row for a converted block.

claims.text: DMA (direct memory access) moves the staging buffer to the FPGA card; the cache's DMA allocation creates the kv_blocks; a view's dma flag says whether its memory is DMA-safe.

fields.definition: Direct memory access: the transfer engine that moves the staging buffer to the FPGA card. The cache's DMA allocation (operator new[]) creates the kv_block objects (Note [KV block lifetime]). A view's dma=true means memory allocated in the DMA address space with zero-filled padding; dma=false means definitely not DMA-safe.

claims.text: The FPGA is the attention accelerator card (field-programmable gate array); HBM is its device memory.

fields.definition: FPGA: field-programmable gate array, the card that runs hardware attention. HBM: High Bandwidth Memory, the FPGA's device memory that holds the staged K/V.

claims.text: Main helpers are threads 1 .. n_workers - 1 of a generated plugin that are idle while main runs save_k; run_main_help calls save_k with the helper's worker_ix so every thread claims work units.

fields.definition: Helper threads of the main thread in generated plugins (worker_ix 1 .. n_workers - 1; worker_ix 0 is main). They are idle while main runs save_k, so run_main_help calls save_k at the same statement position and each helper claims work units of the shared K store.

claims.text: Attention workers are the threads that run the attention kernels; their pending sections wait behind save_k, and they read a pending page only after every minibatch that writes it counted its latch down.

fields.definition: The threads that run the attention kernels of a layer. Their pending sections wait behind save_k. help_drain_gof runs on them. They read a pending page only after every minibatch that writes it counted its latch down, so they are never the reader of a half-saved block.

claims.text: A work unit is a run of consecutive minibatch items inside one 16-token block of one page with the same token_jobs_do_kv value; threads claim units with fetch_add on next_unit.

fields.definition: A run of consecutive items of the minibatch inside one 16-token block of one page with the same token_jobs_do_kv value. Main cuts the item list into units (k_store_cut_units, unit_start[]); every thread claims units with fetch_add on next_unit and stores the rows of each unit it claims (store_k_block).

claims.text: A window (batch::k_store_window) is one shared save_k of a pass: main opens it with a release increment of `opened`, helpers wait for `opened` >= W with acquire, claim units, and increment `finished`.

fields.definition: One shared save_k of a pass. Main resets next_unit and finished, then increments `opened` (release); a helper's W-th call waits for `opened` >= W (acquire); each helper increments `finished` (release) when its claim loop ends and main returns when finished == n_workers - 1 (acquire). Window W is the W-th shared save_k of that pass on both sides.

claims.text: Acquire and release are memory orders: a release store publishes the writes before it, and an acquire load that reads that value sees those writes. The K bits are published with release and read with acquire.

fields.definition: std::memory_order_release on a store or fetch_or makes every write before it visible to a thread whose std::memory_order_acquire load reads the stored value. note_k_block_saved publishes the block bit with release; page::k_vnni_blocks reads it with acquire; acq_rel on fetch_or does both.

claims.text: The tree lock is held during token-tree work between forward passes; while it is held no forward pass reads the book, so the in-place transposes of clear_kv_complete_at and copy_from see no reader.

fields.definition: The lock on the token tree that is held for tree work (clear_kv_complete_at, copy_from, defrag) between forward passes. While it is held no forward pass reads the book, which is the rule the in-place block transposes of those operations rely on.

claims.text: book::fill_random is a test-only whole-block random fill that bypasses the typed access rules: it interprets no coordinates and marks no token complete.

fields.definition: A test-only fill of every kv_block with random bf16 values. It is the one documented exception to the typed packed-K and packed-V access rules: it interprets no coordinates and marks no token complete.

claims.text: Note [KV block lifetime] explains why k_vnni_tensor is a trivial owner with no initialization: the DMA allocation's operator new[] creates the kv_block objects, which works only while kv_block and its members stay trivial.

fields.definition: The cache reads each arena as arrays of kv_block objects whose lifetime the DMA allocation's operator new[] starts. That requires kv_block::k (a bf16 array or the trivially copyable owner k_vnni_tensor) to stay trivial to construct and destroy; the accessors assert it, and SIMD addresses inside a packed plane come from detail::k_vnni_access.

claims.text: detail::k_vnni_access::plane is the one route from a k_vnni_view to its plane address, for the typed operations, the two score kernels and fill_random.

fields.definition: A friend helper with one static function, plane(view), that returns the view's raw pointer to the plane's first element (panel (step 0, block 0), pair row 0, token 0). It is the only route to a packed address, for the operations of this header, qk_group, qk_vnni_128x4 and the test-only fill_random.

claims.text: k_vnni_tensor owns the 16 KiB plane (64-byte aligned, trivial) and k_vnni_view is its typed matrix view with at(token, dim) and no element write; kv_block::k is the owner for a VNNI slot.

fields.definition: k_vnni_tensor<64, 128>: the owner of one packed K plane, one 64-byte-aligned bf16 array with no separate allocation. k_vnni_view<T, 64, 128>: the matrix view that knows the address formula, read through at(token, dim), written only through store_row, store_block, copy_token and the row-major helpers. Views come only from an owner's as_view().

claims.text: page::k_packed is the read-only k_vnni_view of a page's plane for one slot and KV head, handed to qk_vnni_128x4 and qk_group.

fields.definition: The read-only typed view (k_vnni_view<const bf16, 64, 128>) of one page's K plane for a slot and KV head, VNNI slots only. The AMX kernel qk_vnni_128x4 reads it in place as its B operand; the AVX-512 reader qk_group reads it one token per lane. Only the blocks named by k_vnni_blocks hold the VNNI layout in it.

claims.text: A transpose in registers (transpose_16x16_epi32) turns 16 token rows of 16 dwords into 16 pair rows of 16 tokens, in four stages of 16 two-register shuffles.

fields.definition: An in-place transpose of a 16 x 16 matrix of 32-bit lanes held in 16 AVX-512 registers: on return r[i] holds lane i of every input register. Four stages (unpacklo/unpackhi 32-bit, unpacklo/unpackhi 64-bit, two rounds of _mm512_shuffle_i32x4 with EVEN_QUARTERS_0X88 / ODD_QUARTERS_0XDD), 64 shuffles in all. store_block uses it per dimension step.
